records.name: Ofēlija
records.facts_used: Ofēlija: The Latvian form belongs to the Ofelia/Ophelia family. Greek ōpheleia means help or benefit. The name is also familiar in literature, but explaining its root and documenting the particular Latvian form are distinct kinds of evidence. Siliņš’s dictionary dates the use of Ofēlija: the first quarter of the twentieth century. This records use of the particular name in Latvia. The entry cannot automatically be transferred to similar spellings or treated as the moment the entire name family originated.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Siliņš p253 exact Greek help/benefit root and own firstquarter20c; agency exact English Ophelia→Ofēlija Ahero 2006p114. No invented exact local first year.

records.name: Gilmintas
records.facts_used: Gilmintas: The Lithuanian compound is explained through gil-, connected with gilus, deep or strong, and mint-, connected with minti and mintis, thought. These are lexical explanations of separate stems. They need not be turned into one invented sentence as the name’s sole meaning. The 1964 calendar reprinted in Salys’s 1983 volume gives Gilmintas (Gilas) on 12 December. This is a concrete printed example of the form’s use. Its position in the historical calendar need not match every modern calendar and is not the name’s invention date.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Guide explicit two stems; original Salys PDF p. 318/printed p. 303 December12 Gilmintas(Gilas). Calendar reprint is dated use rather than invention.

records.name: Joana
records.facts_used: Joana: The name belongs to the Johannes/Johanna family. Its Hebrew base Yohanan expresses God has been gracious. Feminine forms and renderings in different languages developed at different times; shared ancestry does not give them an identical local history. The medieval name dictionary records related Latin Johanna in England in 1246. This is an earlier example of the international family, rather than the first registration of this local spelling.
records.reason: Exact-form or explicitly scoped family evidence supports two paragraphs in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Exact guide bridge: Joana feminine Jonas; Žana French equivalent Jonė; Žaneta derived Žana. DMNES England Latin Johanna 1246(PSS-IIp6) is explicitly a related-form foreign episode, not first Lithuanian registration.
